chapter_title: Concerning the Light Mind, why it does not exercise Foreknowledge for the Saint as for the Apostle?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by later dialogical framing and community-directed, practical/ethical reasoning about why the Light Mind does not grant foreknowledge to the elect. It repeatedly maps cosmological language (Light Mind) onto ecclesial roles (apostle/elect/holy church) and contemporary risks (dissension, profit, magicians/fortune-tellers), rather than giving an impersonal, systematic cosmos→cosmos exposition. No recoverable correspondential substrate appears.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic Q&A setup: “Once again… questioned the apostle”. The content is explicitly church/institutional (“holy church”, “faithful and the elect”, “apostle”), i.e., cosmos→community application rather than systematic cosmology.

Dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle says…”) introduces community-directed instruction about what the Light Mind can do ‘among the faithful’ and why the elect cannot bear it. This is didactic/pastoral application to roles (elect/faithful), not substrate exposition.
Practical institutional rationale (humility, status rivalry: ‘they would have become an apostle’)—a community-governance concern, not cosmological mechanics.
Ethical/social consequences (despising one another; revealing counsels; ‘shames of their body’)—application to communal relations; no cosmos→cosmos mapping.

Community-psychological warning about disputes; ‘flesh’ and personified Sin language is used to explain interpersonal hostility, i.e., applied moral governance rather than systematic cosmological description.
Continues pragmatic warning (lifespan knowledge leading to abandonment of righteousness). Even with eschatological vocabulary, it functions as behavioral deterrent, not structural cosmology.
Explicit contemporary-world application: disclosure to “magicians… fortune-tellers” for money and “worldly riches” (cosmos→present-world polemic). This is a classic application layer.

Summative rationale addressed to the elect; foreknowledge deferred ‘until the time when they will come forth from their body’—still framed as policy for the community rather than impersonal cosmological architecture.
Concluding promise of total unveiling after leaving the body; eschatological encouragement in the same pastoral explanatory thread, not a distinct, older correspondential unit.
